citation.title: Hierarchical thermal design for battery packs using phase change materials
citation.authors: Matei Ignuta-Ciuncanu, Monica Marinescu, Ricardo Martinez-Botas
citation.venue: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer
citation.version_coded: Version of record metadata/abstract (full text inaccessible)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: At cell scale, the generative latent-space design uses over 95% fewer design variables than conventional pixel-wise topology optimization.
claim.key_phrase: over 95% compared to conventional pixel-wise topology optimization
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: The abstract quantifies design-variable reduction, not a runtime or speed-up factor.
claim.alternatives: Abstract also reports hotspot reductions up to 28.5% at module scale and 60% at pack scale, with pack pumping power at 20% of the uniform-layout requirement.

baseline.problem_size: Design-variable count reduced by over 95% versus pixel-wise topology optimization (abstract)
baseline.quality_metric: Design variables; hotspot temperature; pumping power (abstract)
baseline.quality_gap: Up to 28.5% lower module hotspot temperature without added weight; 60% lower pack hotspot temperature versus lowest-pumping-power design (abstract)

reporting.n_test_cases: Three levels (cell, module, pack); total cases unclear from abstract
